acme-cs: Hey team — starting ~2026-01-15T14:11:22Z we saw a spike of 429s from our production service hitting /v1/chat. Small window but affects a handful of customers. Example request ids we captured: rId=acme-abc123-20260115-141122, rId=acme-abc124-20260115-141130, rId=acme-abc125-20260115-141133. Can you help collect repro evidence and confirm if this is a quota issue?

alex_support: Sorry about that — we'll triage. Can you paste one full raw response (headers + body) for one of the request ids? Also share the exact timestamps in your logs for the three ids (UTC).

acme-cs: Pasted one raw response below from our client (redacted keys):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:11:22 GMT
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 30
X-Request-Id: acme-abc123-20260115-141122
x-rate-limit-limit: 600
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1673783482

Body: {"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit","param":null}}

alex_support: Thanks — that header set is helpful. Two quick asks: 1) can you run a curl reproduction using a dedicated X-Request-Id header so we can correlate? e.g.

curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Request-Id: repro-acme-1779123456" \n  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":32}'

and paste the full response. 2) Collect a HAR from the client for the 14:10:00–14:13:00 UTC window if possible.

acme-cs: Running the curl now, will paste output. Also we can upload a HAR but might need instructions for our infra proxy (nginx).

sara_eng: For HAR from behind nginx: enable proxy logging for the window, or use the browser HAR if this is from a web client. If you want a debug bundle for us, run our internal tool: 

redwood-debug collect --org acme-inc --request-ids acme-abc123-20260115-141122,acme-abc124-20260115-141130 --include har,logs,env --out acme-debug-1779123456.tar.gz

(If you can't run that, upload the raw nginx access+error logs for the timeframe and the client logs that include timestamps and request ids.)

acme-cs: Curl output (redacted auth):
* Connected to api.redwood.com (34.120.12.8) port 443 (#0)
> POST /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
> Accept: */*
> Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED]
> X-Request-Id: repro-acme-1779123456
> Content-Type: application/json
> Content-Length: 82

< HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
< Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 14:11:22 GMT
< Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
< Retry-After: 30
< X-Request-Id: acme-abc123-20260115-141122
< x-rate-limit-limit: 600
< x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
< x-rate-limit-reset: 1673783482

{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded","type":"rate_limit"}}

alex_support: That aligns with the header you pasted earlier. Two possibilities: a per-account per-minute quota hit (token-bucket) or a localized short-term burst from a retry loop. Tim — can you check infra-side token-bucket logs for acme-inc between 14:10–14:13?

tim_ml: Looking now. I can see a short burst of requests from acme's IPs at 14:11:21–14:11:40 that exceeds the configured steady-state limit. The rate limiter shows their bucket drained to 0 at 14:11:22 (matches the Retry-After). I'm pulling the limiter trace and will attach key entries.

deploy-bot: [alert] 2026-01-15T14:11:22Z quota-exceeded org=acme-inc rate_limit=600 window=60s requests=740 peak_per_second=45

alex_support: Good catch. acme-cs — it looks like your service sent ~740 requests in that minute; our quota was 600/min and max burst capacity was exhausted. Can you confirm if you had any retry policy that may amplify failures? e.g., aggressive exponential backoff disabled or zero jitter?

acme-cs: We do have retries but they are linear with no jitter for 5 retries. Backoff is small (200ms). We suspected our client code might retry on timeout and that could pile on.

sara_eng: That retry pattern will magnify a short outage. For repro evidence please: 1) share your client retry config and a short trace showing retry timestamps (with request ids), 2) upload the HAR or nginx logs, 3) run the redwood-debug collect command if possible so we get server-side traces correlated to those request ids.

acme-cs: We'll collect and upload the nginx access logs and the client trace. One quick ask — can you confirm what headers we should look for in responses to prove this is quota and not an auth issue?

alex_support: Sure — key headers are x-rate-limit-limit, x-rate-limit-remaining, x-rate-limit-reset, Retry-After, and X-Request-Id. If x-rate-limit-remaining is 0 on an error and Retry-After is present that's incontrovertible for quota enforcement. Auth errors will be 401/403 and have no x-rate-limit-remaining=0 pattern.

tim_ml: Also check for consecutive 429s with similar x-rate-limit-reset timestamps across different request ids — that shows a shared bucket. I recommend you patch your client to add jitter and longer exponential backoff (e.g., start 500ms, factor 2, max 8s).

acme-cs: Uploading logs now: S3 link (private): https://acme-s3.internal/acme-debug-1779123456.tar.gz (contains nginx access for 14:09–14:15 and our client trace).

alex_support: Received the bundle, starting correlation run. We'll verify request ids against the limiter traces and send a short timeline. If this is quota-only we can suggest a short-term bump or advise retry/backoff changes.

acme-cs: Thanks — appreciate the speedy help. We'll also schedule a deploy with jittered backoff later today and report back. :thumbsup:

alex_support: Thanks — I'll post the correlation results in this thread once I have them.

tim_ml: Correlation complete: all three request ids map to the same token-bucket drain event at 14:11:22Z. Attaching limiter trace snippet (pasted):
[limiter] 14:11:21.983 id=acme-abc123 tokens_before=2 tokens_after=0 requests_in_minute=742 limit=600
[limiter] 14:11:22.879 id=acme-abc124 tokens_before=0 reject=429

alex_support: Final recommendation for now: 1) short-term: request a quota increase for acme-inc while they fix clients (we can do an emergency bump to 900/min for 24h), 2) medium: client changes (jittered exponential backoff), 3) long-term: consider Dedicated capacity if they need sustained higher throughput.

acme-cs: We'll take the emergency bump and push the client fix. Please open the quota bump and confirm here.

alex_support: Bump request submitted to infra team, tracking id infra-qb-7892. Will update when approved.

acme-cs: Thanks all, uploading updated client config after deploy.

sara_eng: Noted — closing triage once bump is confirmed and logs show no recurrence.

acme-cs: Confirmed: infra approved bump infra-qb-7892 -> quota set to 900/min for 24h. We'll monitor and follow up.

alex_support: Great — marking this thread as resolved but keep us posted if 429s reappear.
